questions.question: The Brundtland Commission's definition of sustainable development is development that:
options: Meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
Maximises GDP growth in every year
Bans all use of natural resources
Prioritises the environment above jobs in all cases

questions.question: A tannery's effluent forces downstream families to boil water and visit the clinic. In economic terms these costs are:
options: Part of the tannery's private costs
Externalities — real costs borne by people outside the tannery's transactions, so its product is priced too cheaply
Transfer payments
Sunk costs

questions.question: Clean air is a public good because it is:
options: Free to produce
Supplied by government factories
Non-excludable and non-rival — nobody can be fenced out, and one person's breathing leaves others' undiminished
Traded on world markets

questions.question: Divers race an unowned abalone bed to depletion, each reasoning that whatever they spare another boat will take. This illustrates:
options: Comparative advantage
The free-rider problem in reverse
Demand-pull inflation
The tragedy of the commons — what everybody owns, nobody protects

questions.question: South Africa is described as DOUBLY exposed to climate change because:
options: Its coal-heavy economy is carbon-intensive, while its region warms at roughly double the global average
It has two coastlines
Its population is growing in two provinces only
It imports both oil and gas

questions.question: South Africa's water profile is precarious because the country:
options: Has no dams
Receives about half the world's average rainfall while rivers carry mine drainage, sewage and fertiliser runoff
Exports most of its water
Relies entirely on desalination

questions.question: Biodiversity is treated as economic capital because:
options: Species can be taxed
It appears on the JSE
It is the genetic source of future medicines and crops, and the living inventory tourism sells to the world
It replaces the need for farming

questions.question: The economic reading of environmental damage is that it represents:
options: A cost only to future governments
A moral issue with no monetary dimension
A problem confined to rich countries
Future GDP leaking away — failed harvests, deterred tourists, sick workers and rebuilt cities

subtopics.title: Making Sustainability Pay: the Policy Toolkit

questions.question: Which list contains ONLY command-and-control measures?
options: Emission standards, environmental impact assessments, fishing quotas, water-use licences
The carbon tax, the plastic-bag levy, the tyre levy
Solar rebates and renewable procurement
Tradable permits and eco-labels

questions.question: South Africa's carbon tax, in force since 2019, works by:
options: Banning coal power stations outright
Pricing each ton of carbon dioxide, so every firm saves money continuously by emitting less
Subsidising petrol
Fining only firms caught by inspectors

questions.question: In a tradable permit scheme, the environmental outcome is guaranteed by:
options: The trading between firms
The price of the permits
The CAP on total pollution — trading merely finds the cheapest firms to make the cuts
Voluntary corporate pledges

questions.question: Giving a community legal ownership of its wildlife cures the commons because:
options: It removes all hunting
It transfers the problem to government
Tourists prefer community-owned parks
The asset gains a defender — an animal that funds the village clinic is an animal the village guards

questions.question: The Montreal Protocol of 1987 is cited as the existence proof for environmental cooperation because:
options: The world phased out ozone-destroying CFCs, substitutes were found, and the ozone layer is measurably healing
It created the carbon tax
It ended acid rain in one year
Every country paid identical penalties

questions.question: The three instruments produced at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit were:
options: The Kyoto targets, the Paris pledges and the loss-and-damage fund
Agenda 21, the Convention on Biological Diversity, and the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
The carbon tax, the plastic levy and the tyre levy
The IMF, the World Bank and the UNDP

questions.question: The design contrast between Kyoto (1997) and Paris (2015) is that:
options: Kyoto was voluntary for all; Paris binds only rich nations
Both imposed identical binding cuts on every country
Kyoto was binding but only for developed countries; Paris is universal but built on self-set, voluntary pledges
Paris abolished the UNFCCC

questions.question: South Africa's Just Energy Transition Partnership, announced at Glasgow, involves:
options: A ban on all coal exports from 2025
An IMF structural adjustment loan
The sale of Eskom to foreign investors
Wealthy nations pledging 8,5 billion dollars to help decarbonise without abandoning coal workers and coal towns

questions.question: The brick kiln's books look superb while the village suffers because:
options: Its largest production cost — the downstream damage — is paid by families who appear nowhere in its books
The kiln pays too much tax
Bricks are priced too high
The village overstates its losses

questions.question: The river is abused in a way no one's own garden would be because:
options: Rivers are naturally dirty
The garden has an owner who defends it, while the river belongs to everybody and so nobody can send the bill
Gardens are protected by law and rivers are not
The kiln owns the river

questions.question: The village collection to move the kiln's chimney never fills because:
options: The chimney cannot be moved
The kiln refuses permission
Cleared air would reach every household including non-payers, so each household waits for the others to pay — free riding
The villagers cannot agree on a builder

questions.question: The one-line diagnosis of market-driven environmental damage is:
options: People are naturally wasteful
Firms are run by the wrong managers
Government owns too little land
The damage is priced at zero — so the market produces too much of it

questions.question: The weakness of the RULE (command and control) as a price tag is that:
options: The inspector must keep returning, and a firm that could clean up cheaply has no reason to beat the minimum
Rules are always unconstitutional
Rules only apply to small firms
Fines are paid by consumers directly

questions.question: A pollution TAX 'polices itself' because:
options: Tax officials visit weekly
Every barrel not dumped becomes money saved, so the firm's own bookkeeper watches the pipe every day
Firms fear public shaming
The tax is collected in advance

questions.question: In the toolkit, the tax and the subsidy relate as:
options: Identical instruments with different names
Substitutes that can never be combined
Push and pull — the tax pushes against the old habit while the reward pulls toward the new one
Temporary and permanent versions of the same rule

questions.question: The antelope that pays the village school fees illustrates:
options: The failure of conservation
Why wildlife should be exported
The superiority of state ownership
Property rights curing the commons — an owned asset gains a community of defenders

questions.question: Climate negotiation is called the planet-scale free-rider problem because:
options: Every nation's pipe drains into one shared atmosphere, and each is tempted to let the others pay for the clean-up
Airlines are the biggest emitters
Only islands suffer climate harm
Treaties are written in one language

questions.question: Kyoto's core design lesson was that:
options: Voluntary pledges always fail
Binding homework for the rich alone cannot bend a global curve when the biggest and fastest-growing emitters sit outside it
Emission cuts are technically impossible
Ozone and carbon require one treaty

questions.question: Three additions from the recent climate summits are:
options: A world carbon bank, a green army and an ocean tax
The end of the UNFCCC, new Kyoto targets and a coal subsidy
A coal phase-down agreement, a loss-and-damage fund, and a global stocktake urging a move away from fossil fuels
Binding penalties for all developing countries

questions.question: The word JUST in South Africa's energy transition means:
options: The transition happens quickly
Only the courts manage the process
Coal must be phased out within a year
Coal workers are retrained and coal towns given new industries while the grid turns green — the social leg of sustainability
